question: to the Commission Kathleen Funchion (The Left) Subject:

The Commission has announced that a European Care Deal will be published in 2027, but a genuine timeline is absent. A European Care Deal has the potential to improve care for vulnerable members of our communities across the EU. Particularly in Ireland, where the health service is faced with what is essentially an annual trolly crisis. Such crises are often exacerbated by a lack of public care services outside of a hospital setting. 1.
Does the Commission agree that a sufficient workforce is fundamental to the provision of safe and high-quality care?

Does the Commission agree that collective bargaining can improve the situation for carers in our communities, making a career in care more attractive and thus increasing the number of persons entering and staying in this sector?
Will the Commission’s Care Deal include (binding) commitments to improvements in the sector?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.8.2026) The Commission agrees with the fact that ensuring a skilled workforce in the care sector is key to providing affordable and quality care. The European Care Strategy1 adopted in 2022 aims to ensure quality, affordable and accessible care services while supporting formal and informal carers. The Council Recommendation on access to affordable high-quality long-term care2 (LTC) sets out a comprehensive policy framework and the national implementation plans3 showcase numerous investments and reforms to address workforce challenges. Analytical evidence 45 and the large-scale skills partnership for LTC under the Pact for Skills6 further strengthen the professionalisation of workforce. Improving the working conditions for the LTC workforce needs to be supported by effective collective bargaining. At social partners’ request, the Commission set up in 2023 the European Sectoral Social Dialogue Committee for social services7 to improve working conditions, ensure affordable high quality social services and promote higher standards in care services. A key milestone was the adoption of the Joint Framework of Action on staff retention and recruitment in social services8 in June 2025. The Commission’s renewed commitment to social dialogue and collective bargaining was confirmed in the Pact for European Social Dialogue9 signed by the Commission and EU cross-industry social partners in 2025. Preparatory work on the European Care Deal is underway and it will be presented in 2027.
